content: Objective to use case to product decision to contract to delivery to consumption to evidence to outcome to value to investment decision.
Increase renewal revenue by improving retention intervention decisions.
Reduce manual reporting cost through a governed reusable product.
Improve service recovery by identifying customers with unresolved service interactions.
Meet a regulatory reporting obligation with traceable source, approval and control evidence.
Reduce operational risk by detecting failed product commitments before an affected decision.
Improve access to an eligible public service through timely, accountable information.
Analyst identifies customers at churn risk within 30 days.
Reporting team prepares a controlled regulatory submission.
Support agent finds permitted customer-support context before answering a governed question.
Operations team prioritises service recovery from current service interactions.
Create a product only after reuse alternatives, cost, owner and demand are evaluated.
Extend Customer 360 rather than create a duplicate churn-risk product.
Lifecycle decisions include merge, maintain, deprecate and retire based on evidence.
An individual product contract is validated against the ODPS 4.2 schema.
Catalog references, use cases and business objectives are represented by ODPC objects.
A graph connects objectives, use cases, products, policy and workflow context.
Controlled terms distinguish customer and service interaction meanings.
A portable recipe validates release artifacts before an external human approval gate.
Missing production approval and unresolved entitlement are findings, not inferred compliance states.
Evidence links a claim to a source, capability and period.
Completeness of 94.7 percent fails the declared 98 percent threshold.
Production version 2.3 differs from declared contract version 2.4.0.
Outcome movement, adoption, cost and confounding factors inform a continuation decision.
Agent discovers candidates, reads contracts, resolves vocabulary, checks permissions and returns path evidence.
Denied access, stale product, ambiguous vocabulary, missing relationship, failed quality gate and human approval are stopping or escalation conditions.
